title: How Much Fiber in Edamame? 8.1g per Cup
description: Edamame: about 8.1 g of fiber per 1 cup, shelled, cooked (29% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in edamame?

answer.detail: fiber in 1 cup, shelled, cooked (155 g)
answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Edamame, frozen, prepared

intro: Edamame ranks #9 of 10 beans and legumes on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in edamame by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in edamame?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists edamame, frozen, prepared at 5.2 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup, shelled, cooked; 155 g) therefore has about 8.1 g of fiber and 188 calories. That is 29% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 32% of a 25 g day and 21% of a 38 g day.
Edamame are young green soybeans. They pair a solid amount of fiber with more protein per cup than most beans, which makes them a popular snack for people trying to feel full on fewer calories.

sections.heading: In the pod vs shelled
paragraphs: The figures here are for shelled beans. Edamame served in the pod look like a bigger portion than they are, because you do not eat the pods. A cup of pods yields roughly half a cup of beans.
Frozen shelled edamame (often sold as mukimame) is the easiest form for bowls and salads. Boil or microwave per the package and log the cooked shelled weight.

sections.heading: How edamame compares with other beans and legumes
paragraphs: Of the 10 beans and legumes on this site, edamame ranks #9 for fiber per typical serving and #9 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 4.3 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [green peas](/fiber-in-green-peas) at 8.8 g (1 cup, cooked); [kidney beans](/fiber-in-kidney-beans) at 11.3 g (1 cup, cooked); [chickpeas](/fiber-in-chickpeas) at 12.5 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), edamame is #28 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding edamame to your day
paragraphs: Add a half cup of shelled edamame to a rice bowl, stir-fry, or salad, or keep a bag of frozen pods for a quick salted snack.

Example: 1 cup edamame, 1 cup brown rice, 1 cup broccoli. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 16.4 g of fiber, with 8.1 g from the edamame. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of edamame?
faqs.a: 5.2 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Edamame, frozen, prepared). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in edamame (1/2 cup, shelled, cooked)?
faqs.a: About 4 g, for 77.5 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: Is edamame high in protein too?
faqs.a: Yes. USDA lists cooked shelled edamame at roughly 11–12 g of protein per 100 g, which is more than most cooked beans.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in a bowl of edamame pods?
faqs.a: Count the beans, not the pods. A restaurant appetizer bowl often holds about half a cup to one cup of beans once shelled. Use the shelled rows above.
